findings.summary: The initial exact-parallel assertion assumed cross-build equality for [1,2,3] x [±2,±4,±6]. Actual tspice Node/WASM and the pinned native archive returned zero while the fingerprinted locked macOS arm64 SpiceyPy library returned unit ∓z. The pinned-source and oracle-disassembly investigation attributes this to fused-arithmetic cancellation residuals amplified by normalization, rather than an adapter or mapping defect. Poorly conditioned nonparallel inputs can also differ.
findings.repair: Repaired the assertion strategy: retain the failing input/results and reproduction in the numerical note, use exactly representable dyadic pairs for the computed-zero branch, and retain all mixed, handedness, scaled and axis-based near-parallel cases. Public JSDoc records the conditioning caveat. No scientific implementation, compiler setting, oracle output, global tolerance or routine eligibility is changed. The finding concerns the assertion assumption; it does not claim cross-build equality at the documented ill-conditioned inputs. Fresh source-bound local and CI verification remain separate requirements.
